verdicts.strongest_argument: The facts are right and the arithmetic essentially checks, but this is not an XBRL/10-Q discovery at all — MongoDB put the entire package in its own Q1 FY27 earnings press release on 2026-05-28: 'RPO $1,458.6 million, up 88% year-over-year', 'cRPO $766.3 million, up 69% year-over-year', and non-current deferred revenue $91.2 million are all headline line items in that release, and the CFO quantified it verbally on the call ('ended the period at $1.46 billion... year over year growth of 88% with the current portion growing'). Wire copy carried it as 'backlog up 88%'. The hunter's derived '+72% next-12-month committed revenue' is in fact a slightly worse restatement of a company-disclosed +69% cRPO, computed from the duration-mix percentages rather than the disclosed dollar figure. More damaging for the mechanism: the FY27 raise the finding says is 'mechanically available' has already happened — the same 2026-05-28 release lifted FY27 to $2.92-2.96bn WITH the +88% RPO in hand, and the stock moved +3.03%. The market has seen this exact backlog number alongside a raise and repriced for it; the subsequent +23% 20-day and +32% one-month run-up on AI-workload momentum, with targets lifted to $475 (Truist) and $525 (Evercore), means the strong-visibility read is now the consensus going in, not the variant. The only sliver not drawn out anywhere is the 10-Q duration-mix footnote (46% in 13-36 months vs 38%), i.e. that the lengthening is where the growth sits — worth a few points off 100, no more. Note also management's own caveat that 'it remains difficult to predict the duration of our EA deals', which cuts against treating RPO as a clean forward multiplier for a consumption business.

prior_publication.what_it_says: MongoDB's own Q1 FY27 release discloses RPO $1,458.6m up 88% YoY, cRPO $766.3m up 69% YoY, and non-current deferred revenue $91.2m, alongside the raised FY27 guidance of $2.92-2.96bn.

CFO Mike Berry states RPO 'ended the period at $1.46 billion... year over year growth of 88%', explains it is mostly existing enterprise customers, and caveats that EA deal duration is difficult to predict.
The same release as Exhibit 99.1 to the Q1 FY27 earnings 8-K, so the figures are in an SEC-filed company source, not just a footnote.
Trade coverage of the Q1 print leads with 'revenue up 25%, backlog up 88%' — the RPO growth was in the wire narrative the day it was released.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The information became public on 2026-05-28 and the baseline records that event's reaction as +3.03%, so the market absorbed the +88% RPO and the FY27 raise together for a 3% move. Since then spot is +23.17% over 20d and only -6.64% from the 52w high, i.e. the bullish visibility story has been bid up, not ignored. The 25-delta skew of -0.17 vol points is essentially symmetric, so I explicitly cannot claim the market has taken a bullish directional stance for this finding to agree with — my case rests on publication and on the 2026-05-28 reaction, not on skew. What the options do say is magnitude: a 14.49% event-implied move is the bar, and a prior-quarter disclosed backlog metric is not plausibly worth that.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the RPO surge came from a single dated multi-year commitment whose recognition start falls inside May-July 2026 in a size not contemplated by the $729-734m Q2 guide, and that no sell-side model has that revenue in it.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every component of this is published, most of it in wire copy, and one component moved the price by 22% on the day it landed. Cedric Pech's resignation was disclosed in the 8-K filed 2026-03-02 — the same 8-K as the Q4 FY26 Item 2.02 results, i.e. the print the baseline records at -22.24%; so the market's single largest negative MDB reaction in eight events already had the field-leadership departure inside it. The Mac Ban appointment and the exact 'Capombassis will support a seamless transition to Mac Ban through Q2' language went out on PR Newswire, Reuters and Investing.com on 2026-03-24. The two new CPOs were named on 2026-04-22 and re-narrated by management on the 2026-05-28 call. The finding's *mechanism* has also been written out explicitly in public: Simply Wall St's April note says leadership transitions at the top of sales 'can lead to short term disruption in deal cycles, territory alignment, or sales incentives, which may affect how quickly MongoDB converts AI related interest into signed contracts', and TheStreet's 2026-05-20 BofA piece states that the simultaneous CRO and President-Field-Operations departures 'added to investor concern about near-term sales execution' and that this combination helped drive a 20% YTD decline. And management pre-empted the specific risk on the record on the Q1 call: 'we felt very confident in terms of making sure that there was not going to be any... changes to comp plans... I would not expect any significant changes for the remainder of fiscal 2027'. Where I stop short of 90: I accept the fact and I accept the sign is at least available, but I found no piece that assembles the four moves into 'the quarter being reported IS the handover quarter' and prices it, and nobody has quantified it. That aggregation is a real, if thin, edge. I do not accept the size implied by framing it as a full 'field-and-product leadership rebuild' — the outgoing CRO stayed on through the quarter by design, the new CRO started 27 Apr with the quarter's pipeline already built, and the sign is genuinely two-sided: a handover quarter is as often sandbagged into a beatable guide as it is missed.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Announces Mac Ban effective 2026-04-27 and states outgoing CRO Capombassis will support the transition through Q2 — the exact sentence the finding relies on, published six months ago.
8-K filed with the Q4 FY26 results (Items 2.02 and 5.02) discloses Cedric Pech's 2026-02-27 notice of resignation as President, Field Operations effective 2026-04-15.
Reuters newswire carried the CRO appointment, so it is literally in the wire copy.
Spells out the mechanism — sales-leadership transition risks short-term disruption to deal cycles, territory alignment and incentives, slowing conversion of AI interest into signed contracts.

BofA note coverage: the simultaneous CRO and President Field Operations departures added to investor concern about near-term sales execution and contributed to a ~20% YTD decline, with BofA arguing the concern is temporary.
Management walks through Mac Ban, the two new CPOs (Cefalo, Stern) and CCO Volini, and the CFO says he does not expect significant comp-plan or go-to-market changes for the remainder of FY27.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The Pech departure was disclosed inside the 2026-03-02 earnings 8-K, and that event's realised reaction is -22.24% in the baseline history — the price demonstrably moved when the leadership story became known, even if bundled with guidance. Since then the stock has recovered to -6.64% from the 52w high with +23.17% over 20 days, which is the market voting that the execution concern faded. The 25-delta skew is -0.17 vol points, i.e. essentially symmetric, so I state plainly that the market has taken NO directional view here and this finding therefore has no priced lean to contradict; equally, nobody is bidding puts for a sales-disruption miss, so the residual is a genuinely open two-sided risk rather than a market blind spot with a sign. Magnitude is the binding constraint: at a 14.49% event-implied move with a 19.58% median historical reaction, an unquantified qualitative handover risk is a small fraction of what is already paid for.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Hiring-data, channel-check or Glassdoor/LinkedIn evidence of quantified May-July field attrition or territory re-carving — something showing the handover actually cost bookings in the reported quarter, rather than that a handover was scheduled during it.

interactions: The two findings rest on the same two documents and point in opposite directions. Both trace to the 2026-05-28 Q1 FY27 earnings event: #0 is the RPO disclosure in that press release, #1 leans on the 2026-03-24 CRO release but its live status is set by the same 2026-05-28 call, where management addressed both items back to back — quantifying RPO at +88% and simultaneously saying it expected no significant go-to-market or comp-plan changes for the rest of FY27. That is awkward for the hunt as a set: #0 argues the backlog makes a bigger raise mechanically available, #1 argues field execution is at risk in the very quarter that backlog is supposed to be converting. They can both be true, but they cannot both be surprises, because the single call that is the primary source for each already juxtaposed them for the market. There is also a partial arithmetic collision: #0's derived '+72% next-12-month committed revenue' is a re-derivation of the company's own disclosed cRPO +69% from the same release, so the finding's headline number is both less accurate and less novel than the disclosure it came from. Neither finding, at my sizes (+2.5% and -3.0%), comes close to the 14.49% event-implied move; taken together they roughly cancel, which is consistent with the symmetric skew and argues against MDB ranking strongly in either direction on this evidence.
